message.content:
**Los Angeles (Pacific Time) vs. Berlin (Central European Time)**  

| Period | Los Angeles | Berlin | Time‑zone offset | Difference |
|--------|-------------|--------|------------------|------------|
| **Standard time** (winter) | UTC‑8 | UTC+1 | 9 hours ahead | **+9 h** |
| **Daylight‑saving time** (summer) | UTC‑7 | UTC+2 | 9 hours ahead | **+9 h** |

### Why it can vary

The U.S. and Europe change daylight‑saving time on **different dates**:

| Transition | U.S. (Pacific) | Europe (Central) | Resulting difference |
|------------|----------------|------------------|----------------------|
| **Early March** | Second Sunday (start DST) | Last Sunday (start DST) | 8 h (Berlin 10 h ahead) |
| **Late October** | First Sunday (end DST) | Last Sunday (end DST) | 8 h (Berlin 10 h ahead) |
| **Late March – Late October** | Both on DST | Both on DST | 9 h |
| **Late October – Early March** | Both on Standard | Both on Standard | 9 h |

So:

- **Most of the year**: Berlin is **9 hours ahead** of Los Angeles.
- **During the brief overlap** when Europe has already switched to DST but the U.S. hasn’t (or vice‑versa), the difference can be **8 or 10 hours**.

If you need the exact difference for a specific date, let me know the date and I can calculate it precisely.
